markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

Three observations motivate the next experiment. First, Electronics has 15.53% sampled training-pair errors, while Movies_and_TV and CDs_and_Vinyl have below 0.35%. This identifies uneven training separation, without establishing validation performance. Second, sampled causal and compatibility-view checks pass. Independently exported predictor parity remains unverified. Third, the existing residual aggregates historical evidence before seeing a candidate. It therefore cannot require the recommended item itself to match recurring interests.

Three related-work insights qualify this direction. Recency research [1] cautions against assuming that stronger recent-item emphasis improves accuracy. Retain older corroboration while testing a fixed decay. Sampled-metric research [2] shows that candidate sampling can change model comparisons. Preserve the pinned objective and distinguish it from full-catalog inspection. TRACE [3] motivates controlled history edits and ranking-margin measurements. Such probes establish model dependence, not user intent.

These insights suggest three directions: candidate-specific evidence, temporal calibration, and diagnostic correctness.

## Framework and alternatives

| Method | Evidence destination | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Learned sequence representation | No explicit corroboration requirement |
| Starting residual | Historical ID-embedding pool | Candidate relevance remains indirect |
| Proposed residual | Individual candidate score | Lexical similarity misses complements |

Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate-specific two-witness score [1,3] | 4/7/4 | Directly tests candidate corroboration | Can suppress emerging interests |
| Two fixed recency scales [1] | 3/6/3 | Cheap temporal flexibility | Adds selection choices |
| Duplicate-text witness grouping [3] | 4/6/5 | Reduces superficial corroboration | Grouping thresholds are arbitrary |

## Selected experiment

At 20% progress, test **candidate-specific two-witness scoring** as one minimal architectural change. Replace the pooling branch with a bounded score residual; keep SASRec and its training settings unchanged.

Fit frozen category-specific TF–IDF using unique training-history items’ titles/descriptions. For candidate i and causal prefix t, let a[j] be its nonnegative text cosine with historical event j, multiplied by exp(−age[j]/20). Define q(i,t) as the maximum min(a[j],a[k]) over witnesses with different item IDs, both different from i, and event separation at least three. Missing or insufficient evidence gives zero. Score with s(i,t)=s_SASRec(i,t)+tanh(alpha)q(i,t), initializing alpha=0. This preserves weak evidence rather than normalizing it upward; confidence is deterministic support, not probability.

Compare unchanged SASRec, this branch, and matched shuffled-text scoring within the shared budget. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Verify causal prefixes, brute-force agreement, and exported scores across all routes; preserve the diagnosis interface. Twenty-user full-catalog inspection remains descriptive. Compatibility, ownership and unmet needs remain unknown unless explicitly supported.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [2] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [3] https://github.com/devUuung/TRACE

idea.description: Replace the history-pooling residual with a bounded candidate-specific lexical corroboration score. Each candidate receives support only from two different historical item identities, separated by at least three retained events and different from the candidate. Add the support through one zero-initialized scalar gate to the unchanged SASRec score.
idea.motivation: The existing branch corroborates historical anchors but does not require a candidate to share that corroborated evidence. Candidate-conditioned scoring directly tests this gap using observed titles, descriptions and interaction histories. The supplied diagnostics show training-ranking weaknesses, especially in Electronics, but provide no evidence that this intervention improves validation HR@10. Lexical agreement cannot establish practical compatibility, ownership, replacement intent or unmet need.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, original splits, single-GPU execution and the environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200. Retain baseline loss, optimizer, embeddings, positional indexing and training allowance for the first comparison. Store every artifact beneath the trial directory. No experiments or filesystem inspection were performed for this proposal.

Fit one TfidfVectorizer per dataset on unique training-history items in stable item-ID order, concatenating title and description. Fix lowercase=True, word unigrams/bigrams, token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', min_df=2, max_features=20000, sublinear_tf=True and norm='l2'; use other sklearn defaults. Freeze and serialize the transform, version, item mapping and sparse item matrix. Transform other public item text without refitting. Missing text maps to zero; an empty vocabulary disables this branch. Do not use the unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories, stores or prices described by the generic input examples.

For candidate i, prefix t and retained valid event j, define a[j]=cosine(text[i],text[item[j]])*exp(-(rank[t]-rank[j])/20). Eligible witnesses j<k<=t must satisfy rank[k]-rank[j]>=3 and have three distinct IDs across i,item[j],item[k]. q(i,t) is the maximum eligible min(a[j],a[k]), or zero. It lies in [0,1]. Return baseline_score(i,t)+tanh(alpha)*q(i,t), with one alpha per dataset initialized to zero. This explicitly replaces the earlier pooling branch; combining both would add a separate experimental factor. A negative learned gate is permitted and must be reported without calling it reinforcement.

Use an exact scan for each candidate-prefix query: maintain the two highest per-ID eligible left-witness maxima and exclude the right witness ID at query time. Decay can be factored as exp(-(t-k)/20)*min(cos(i,j)*exp(-(k-j)/20),cos(i,k)); decay maintained maxima between right-witness steps. This avoids unstable growing exponentials. A direct sparse implementation may be adequate at short retained lengths; profile before committing training budget. Chunk full-catalog scoring and never materialize catalog-by-catalog similarities. Recompute after truncation. Do not silently approximate similarities or retain witnesses outside the current window.

Prespecify baseline, candidate-specific scoring and a matched seed-fixed within-category item-to-text reassignment control. Record settings, checkpoint cadence, identical training allowances and GPU-second allocations before execution. Count failures, profiling, diagnostics and checkpoint evaluation within 43,200 GPU-seconds. If the comparisons cannot fit, report incomplete evidence. Select only with the pinned host macro validation HR@10 over all four categories; report per-category results. Training margins and twenty-user full-catalog recommendations remain auxiliary.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py restores the TF–IDF artifacts, gate and identical candidate scoring. Verify brute-force versus optimized support, unchanged scores at alpha=0, causal prefix invariance, and training-side/exported score parity with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4. Cover missing text, repeated IDs, padding, short prefixes and truncated windows for every route. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module. Because scoring now needs history, adapt log2feats and predict_score together using an explicit structured feature carrier containing base features and exact integer prefix IDs; update probes to inspect learned coordinates and context IDs separately. Avoid mutable last-sequence caches and floating-point packing of IDs. Restore model modes and RNG states after diagnosis, and mark unsupported observations unavailable.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# Preserve baseline preprocessing, routing, training seeds and objective.
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    text = fit_and_freeze_tfidf(unique_training_history_items(dataset))
    model = baseline_sasrec(dataset)
    alpha = Parameter(0.0)

    def candidate_support(prefix, candidate):
        events = retained_valid_events(prefix)
        best = 0.0
        for j in range(len(events)):
            for k in range(j + 3, len(events)):
                if len({candidate, events[j], events[k]}) != 3:
                    continue
                left = cosine(text[candidate], text[events[j]])
                right = cosine(text[candidate], text[events[k]])
                left *= exp(-(len(events) - 1 - j) / 20.0)
                right *= exp(-(len(events) - 1 - k) / 20.0)
                best = max(best, min(left, right))
        return best

    # Above is the reference definition; validate any optimized scan against it.
    for sequence, positive, negative in baseline_training_batches:
        base_features = model.log2feats(sequence)
        for supervised_position t:
            prefix = sequence[:, :t + 1]
            pos_score = baseline_score(base_features[:, t], positive[:, t])
            neg_score = baseline_score(base_features[:, t], negative[:, t])
            pos_score += tanh(alpha) * candidate_support(prefix, positive[:, t])
            neg_score += tanh(alpha) * candidate_support(prefix, negative[:, t])
        optimize_unchanged_baseline_loss_on_valid_positions()

    serialize_model_text_artifacts_and_gate_under_trial_directory()
    update_predictor_writer_with_identical_candidate_scoring()
    verify_exported_score_parity_and_diagnostic_contract()
# Run only budgeted comparisons; select by host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Moves explicit distinct-witness corroboration from a candidate-independent history pool into each candidate's score, producing a clear and falsifiable change.
originality.negative: Content-based scoring, temporal weighting and gated residuals are established techniques; novelty of the exact combination is unverified.

future_potential.positive: Controlled results could clarify when candidate-specific repeated evidence contributes beyond sequential ID modeling and motivate learned evidence requirements.
future_potential.negative: Lexical overlap may favor redundant alternatives, miss useful complements and penalize genuinely new interests; distinct IDs do not ensure independent evidence.

code_difficulty.positive: Only one trainable scalar is added, and the support statistic has an exact, independently checkable definition.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient candidate-conditioned sparse scoring, structured diagnostic features and full-catalog predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes a recency metric and reports accuracy costs from excessive recent-item emphasis in evaluated models.
Motivates testing temporal weighting rather than assuming a shorter interest horizon is better.
limitations: Does not establish a suitable decay constant for these four datasets.
Does not validate the proposed candidate-specific corroboration rule.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons, including in expectation.
Supports distinguishing the mandated sampled-candidate HR@10 objective from full-catalog inspection.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.
Does not predict which proposed architecture will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: TRACE
contributions: The supplied summary describes influence-guided history edits assessed through actual ranking margins.
Motivates matched history perturbations for checking dependence on corroborating events.
limitations: Perturbation sensitivity does not establish causal user preferences.
Its history-editing approach does not directly establish the effectiveness of this scoring residual.
